defects.scenario: armBootGuards() is called at the very top of the whenReady callback (apps/ptah-electron/src/main.ts:122-126), BEFORE bootstrapElectron() runs (main.ts:160), and Sentry is only initialized inside bootstrapElectron (apps/ptah-electron/src/activation/bootstrap.ts:258-271, sentryService.initialize(...) at line 264, calling Sentry.init() via @sentry/node -- libs/backend/vscode-core/src/services/sentry.service.ts:34). Sentry's default integration set installs OnUncaughtException, whose setup() calls global.process.on('uncaughtException', makeErrorHandler(...)) (node_modules/@sentry/node-core/build/cjs/integrations/onuncaughtexception.js:20) -- i.e. AFTER our own boot-guard listener. Node invokes same-event listeners in registration order, so on a real uncaught exception during boot (e.g. an IPC handler throw between whenReady and renderer load, hours-zero not hours-later), OUR handler runs first: it writes one stderr line then calls exit(1) => app.exit(1) inside its finally block (boot-trace.ts:122-128). app.exit() terminates the process immediately and does not return control to the still-pending JS call stack, so Sentry's listener (registered second, per onuncaughtexception.js:39-46's own 'userProvidedListenersCount' check it would have found our handler and deferred to it anyway) NEVER runs its core.captureException(...) call (onuncaughtexception.js line 52). Net effect: every boot-window uncaught exception is now invisible to Sentry -- exactly the failure class this task most wants surfaced -- even though it previously WAS captured (pre-task, with no competing handler, Sentry was the sole 'uncaughtException' listener and both captured and exited). This is a regression introduced specifically by round 1's revision (the original whole-process handler only logged and never called exit, so it never pre-empted Sentry's listener); it directly answers the round-2 brief's own question about app.exit(1) interacting badly with Sentry's handler ordering.
defects.note: Local stderr trace still fires first (so it is not 'silent' by this task's own narrow definition), but remote crash reporting for boot failures is now silently dropped. Fix: call reportBootFailure and any Sentry capture (e.g. a synchronous Sentry.captureException if initialized) before exit, or arm the boot guard's uncaughtException listener AFTER Sentry initializes so Sentry's listener runs first and this handler becomes the exit-authority of last resort.

defects.scenario: The `did-finish-load` `.once` listener that disarms the boot guards (bootStep(RENDERER_LOADED_STEP), lines 92-94) only fires on a SUCCESSFUL renderer load. The sibling `mainWindow.loadFile(rendererPath).catch(...)` at lines 98-100 -- added this round specifically to make a failed renderer load observable -- only calls reportBootFailure(...); it never calls disarmBootGuards(). If the production renderer's index.html fails to load (missing/corrupted build asset, GPU/renderer-process-gone mid-load, disk error), the window itself is not closed -- it just stays showing whatever it last rendered (the preparing-workspace shell), so `window-all-closed` never fires and nothing in main.ts quits the app (unlike the analogous failures for the PREPARING shell at main.ts:149-154, which continues boot, or bootstrapElectron() at main.ts:164-193, which goes to recovery mode -- this is the only failure path added by the round-1 revision with no recovery or disarm). The process is left running indefinitely with the boot-scoped `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` handlers from armBootGuards still attached to `process` (boot-trace.ts:129-130) -- i.e. this reproduces, for the rest of the session, exactly the whole-process-handler regression judge-round-1.json's D1 was raised against and this round's revision claims to have fixed. Concretely: any later, unrelated uncaught exception anywhere in the app (not just during boot) will now hit this stale handler and force `app.exit(1)`, compounding with D1 above by also silently bypassing Sentry for that exception, for the remainder of the session -- not just the boot window.
defects.note: No test exercises this path: apps/ptah-electron/src/activation/post-window.ts has no spec file at all (verified: no post-window*.spec.ts exists), and boot-trace.spec.ts only tests armBootGuards/disarmBootGuards/bootStep in isolation, never the renderer-load-failure integration through post-window.ts. Fix: call disarmBootGuards() (or an equivalent exit/recovery path) in the loadFile().catch() branch, mirroring the recovery-shell path in main.ts.

testsRan: npx nx run-many -t test -p ptah-electron -- --maxWorkers=2 --skip-nx-cache (executed by judge from this worktree): 6/7 dependency build tasks served from cache (unaffected inputs), the `ptah-electron:test` task itself force-run fresh (not cache-hit) and Nx reported 'Successfully ran target test for project ptah-electron and 6 tasks it depends on' with no failures (run duration 1m6s on the test task). This matches implementation-notes.md's own claim of 52 suites / 852 tests passing. boot-trace.spec.ts (read in full) is behavioural against a real EventEmitter substitute and a real `process`, and correctly proves: did-finish-load is wired with `.once` so a renderer reload cannot re-arm or double-disarm; the watchdog is unref'd and its timer count drops to 0 on success; stderr-throw (EBADF/EPIPE) does not prevent exit(1); listenerCount on the real process returns to its pre-boot value after the renderer step. None of the passing tests exercise the Sentry-listener-ordering interaction (D1) or the renderer-load-failure non-disarm path (D2) -- both are integration gaps between boot-trace.ts, post-window.ts and bootstrap.ts that no single file's unit tests can see.
mentorNote: Round 1's D1 (whole-process handlers, never disarmed) is genuinely fixed for the path it was written against: the happy path disarms cleanly, `.once` on did-finish-load makes disarm idempotent across renderer reloads (confirmed by reading post-window.ts:92-94 -- a real concern for e2e's ui.prepare() reload, and it is handled correctly), the watchdog is diagnostics-only and unref'd, and the recovery-shell / bootSequence-rejection paths both call disarmBootGuards() explicitly (main.ts:183, main.ts:334). wire-runtime.ts and post-window.ts's core B1 ordering (startCodeExecutionMcp pre-window, registerCodeExecutionMcpForSubagents in postWindow still before booter.openWindowGate()) is untouched this round -- the diff against bb4077d82 shows only bootStep() trace calls and the did-finish-load/catch wiring added on top of round 1's structure, so round 1's ordering verdict stands. But the round-2 brief's own suspicion about Sentry handler ordering was correct: because armBootGuards() runs before Sentry initializes, and the boot-guard's uncaughtException handler now calls app.exit(1) synchronously (added specifically to fix D1), it pre-empts Sentry's own OnUncaughtException listener every time, so Sentry silently loses every boot-window crash report (D1, this round). And the fix for D1(round1) has an asymmetric gap: of the three failure branches added or touched by the revision (preparing-shell load, bootstrapElectron, renderer load), only the renderer-load failure -- the newest addition, in post-window.ts -- has no disarm/recovery, so it can leave the round-1-fixed whole-process regression back in place for the rest of the session if the production renderer itself fails to load (D2). Both are real, narrow-trigger-but-severe-consequence gaps in code that exists specifically to close round 1's finding, not in the parts round 1 already exercised -- send back for a scoped fix to both before merge.
